question: Do implementations of the value-change models discussed in Paper 1 §§4-6 treat a conversion and an attitudinally identical manipulation alike, and do the §6.8 benchmark and the two ways out of §5.4 behave as the paper says?
verdict: ALL PREDICTIONS MET. Over 1000 random draws: the replica manipulation reproduced the conversion's profile in 1000/1000; each of the 9 attitude-based models gave matched conversion and manipulation the same output in 1000/1000 or more; the counterfactual benchmark gave an unassisted conversion no penalty and an occasioned conversion the same positive penalty as its replica manipulation in 1000/1000 (median penalties S2 1.631, S4 1.631); the target condition separated conversions from manipulations in 1000/1000; the attitude-independent standard scored conversion and benevolent manipulation alike in 1000/1000; Spearman(size of change, Pettigrew aggregate) = -0.850 for conversions and -0.850 for manipulations. P2 holds by construction for profile-only implementations; P4 and P7 are the parts that could have failed.
